text:
Maya: FYI provisioning in ap-south1 is hitting a bunch of nodes that never finish initramfs, looks tied to the kernel bump to 6.6 and the new NV driver package.
Liam: Any logs? which package/version?
Maya: saw this on 3/40 nodes so far. snippet: `modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia': Exec format error` then later `rmmod: ERROR: Module nvidia is in use` right in the initramfs step.
Andre: dkms output when the node boots and chroots: `dkms install -m nvidia -v 572.16 --no-depmod` -> fails to build (symbol versions mismatch). also `dkms status` shows both 550.12 and 572.16 installed for kernel 6.6.0-rc.
Kevin: so leftover module artifacts from previous driver remain and dkms is trying to build new one against different headers. Are we shipping any prebuilt .ko with the image?
Maya: image has prebuilt /lib/modules/<kernel>/updates/nvidia. We tried removing it in a test boot, then dkms builds cleanly. But at initramfs time rmmod can't remove because module is in use by nvidia-modeset/nvidia-drm.
Liam: could be race in initramfs scripts where module included in initramfs and dkms rebuild steps run later. That would make rmmod impossible.
Andre: quick reproduction: boot live image + chroot, run `lsinitramfs /boot/initrd.img-6.6 | grep nvidia` -> returns modules.
Maya: current impact: provisioning stuck (initramfs shell) on approx 7% of new nodes in ap-south1, others unaffected. Affected nodes are all A100s with NVLink enabled.
Kevin: NVLink may bring in extra dependencies (nv_peer_mem?) causing module refs. Also noticed that the fleet's custom provisioning image still contains CUDA 11.8 libs in /opt which expect older driver. Mixed ABI.
Maya: tried quick workaround: in preseed we purge old nvidia packages and remove /lib/modules/*/updates/nvidia before running update-initramfs. That allowed nodes to finish in our test.
Liam: can we push a temporary ansible task to remove any prebuilt nvidia .ko from the initramfs and force dkms to build during provisioning? Danger: if dkms build fails, node will still fail.
Andre: propose two-step mitigation: 1) pin driver package to 550.12 for ap-south1 provisioning image (known-good), 2) add pre-provision cleanup to remove leftover .ko and old dkms entries and ensure kernel-headers match.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: ansible playbook "infra/provisioning/fix-nvidia-initramfs" will run to ap-south1 in 10m.
Kevin: we should also gate further kernel 6.6 image rollouts until we verify dkms for 572 driver across CPU/kernel variants.
Maya: created a quick alert dashboard: count of nodes stuck in initramfs per region + dkms build failures. Linking here: https://internal.monitoring/redwood/dkms-init-failures
Liam: any indication this hits Dedicated / Private customers?
Maya: Private images seem fine (they don't include our prebuilt driver). Dedicated: a handful of nodes where customers pinned drivers reported higher failure rate during provisioning.
Andre: root cause candidate: leftover in-initramfs prebuilt nvidia .ko + mismatched kernel-headers -> dkms tries to compile but module already referenced -> rmmod fails, initramfs drops to shell.
Kevin: immediate actions: (A) pause kernel 6.6 rollout in ap-south1, (B) run the ansible cleanup and pin to 550.12 image, (C) open support ticket with NVIDIA for symbol version mismatch between 550x->572x on our custom image.
Maya: I'll coordinate rollback/pinning and run a 50-node canary after cleanup.
Liam: after canary success we can resume rollout with staged waves + extra dkms logging.
Andre: long-term: bake driver install into image properly (dkms at build time with matching headers), avoid shipping prebuilt .ko in updates/, and add upstream check to our image CI that `lsinitramfs` doesn't include nvidia modules unless intentional.
Maya: noted. I'll file the postmortem ticket and include remediation steps + cost estimate for delayed rollout.
Kevin: thanks. reassigning to @Andre to own the ansible task, @Maya to manage canary and postmortem. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1423 - NVIDIA DKMS/initramfs provisioning stall (ap-south1).
